mechanisms.mechanism: A line that looks like one of the task template's headings counts as a heading wherever it stands, also inside a fenced block or an HTML comment. Two things follow. Where the handoff quotes `## Out of scope` in a fenced block, the hashed text runs on to that line: the decisions and the handoff above the quote are hashed too, the hash changes when one of them is written, and the loop reports a changed request although neither the request nor the criteria changed. And in a task file without an out-of-scope heading of its own, a quoted one inside the criteria ends the hashed text early: a criterion below it can change, and the hash stays the same. A task file whose headings stand only inside a fenced block or a comment is hashed where it should be refused.
mechanisms.trigger: A handoff that quotes the line `## Out of scope` in a fenced block, and then an edit to a decision or to the handoff above that line. Or: criteria that quote that line in a fenced block, in a file with no out-of-scope heading, and then an edit to a criterion below the quote.
mechanisms.why_severity: A probable defect that takes a task file which quotes a heading of the template. It makes the report of a changed request wrong, or lets a changed criterion pass; the review itself is not affected.
